theater: 雅典城與比雷埃夫斯港

battle.name: 公元前411年雅典政變
battle.theater: 雅典城與比雷埃夫斯港
battle.brief: 公元前411年秋，雅典海軍覆沒、國庫空虛，斯巴達軍進駐狄刻利亞，寡頭派在皮山德、忒拉美涅斯主導下奪取議會，成立「四百人議會」，廢除五百人議會，宣稱恢復梭倫祖制並企圖向斯巴達議和。卡面這位重步兵正站在風暴中心：衛城與比雷埃夫斯港公民重步兵拒絕服從寡頭，以集會逼退議會，民主年底復辟。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 這場衝突發生在雅典城邦內部，形式上是一場政變而不是城邦之間的戰爭，因此沒有兩支對等的國家軍隊，參與者分成三個政治板塊。第一個板塊是奪權的寡頭派：以「四百人議會」為核心，成員是雅典城內最富有的公民，四百人按十個部落各出四十名，另設十人籌劃委員會起草新憲制，名義上擁護「梭倫祖制」與「祖傳政體」，同時與斯巴達方面私下接洽，指望以外交條件換取政權的壽命。第二個板塊是城外的民主派：駐紮在薩摩斯島的雅典海軍水手與划槳手，他們拒不解散自己的議事機構，拒絕接受寡頭派指派的將領，一度揚言駕船溯流直指比雷埃夫斯。第三個板塊是外部強權：斯巴達聯軍自公元前413年起駐紮狄刻利亞，扼住阿提卡的陸路；波斯方面則透過提薩斐涅斯與法爾納巴茲同時向雙方下棋，亞西比德正以波斯人的資源充當民主派的棋子。整場政變的勝負，實際由城內公民重步兵的動向決定。
countriesEn: This clash took place inside the polis of Athens and was a coup rather than a war between states, so there were no two equal national armies; the participants divide into three political blocs. The first was the oligarchic faction that seized power: a council of Four Hundred made up of the wealthiest citizens of the city, forty from each of the ten tribes, with a board of ten commissioners appointed to draft a new constitution. It proclaimed adherence to the 'ancestral constitution' of Solon while simultaneously sounding out Sparta, in the hope that diplomatic terms would buy the new regime a longer life. The second bloc was the democratic party in the field: the Athenian crews and oarsmen stationed with the fleet at Samos, who refused to disband their own council of state and refused officers appointed by the oligarchs, and who at one point threatened to sail up the straits to the Piraeus. The third bloc was made up of the outside powers: the Spartan coalition had held Decelea since 413 BC and gripped the land route into Attica, while Persia played both sides through Tissaphernes and Pharnabazus, with Alcibiades using Persian resources on behalf of the democrats. In the end the outcome of the coup was decided by the movements of the citizen heavy infantry inside the city.
people: 主導政變的是皮山德（Pisander）。這位先後兩度擔任雅典使節、外交手腕圓熟的外交官，在公元前411年被派往薩摩斯島的雅典分艦隊，打算說服水手們解散、繳械返航，好讓城內的寡頭派順利接管軍權。他在島上聽到亞西比德（Alcibiades）自流亡地送來的信：信中指寡頭派真正的目的是把雅典拱手交給斯巴達，並提醒水手們，寡頭派一旦在城內得逞，就會廢掉公民的民主身份，隨後把水手押回城裡處置。皮山德說服水手的方式，是先承諾維持口糧與軍餉，卻被水手反過來要求更高的條件，談判破裂之後，皮山德與同來的同僚在艦上被水手殺死。城內方面，忒拉美涅斯（Theramenes）是四百人議會中的溫和派，主張政變只是為了逼人民接受和談；當城內守備與比雷埃夫斯港的公民起義時，他立刻改變立場，勸四百人議會解散，自己則退到廣場的十二神祭壇與衛城尋求庇護，隨後被民主派列入赦免名單。阿里斯托豐（Aristophon）同樣是主張溫和、傾向避免流血的寡頭。站在民主派一邊的，是薩摩斯島的水手、駐守衛城與比雷埃夫斯港的公民重步兵，以及在集市集會上主張廢黜四百人議會的發言者。
peopleEn: The driving figure of the coup was Pisander, a diplomat who had twice served as an Athenian envoy and was skilled in negotiation. In 411 BC he was sent to the Athenian squadron at Samos with the object of persuading the crews to disband and sail home, so that the oligarchs inside the city could take over the armed forces without resistance. On the island he heard a letter from Alcibiades, who was in exile: the letter claimed that the real purpose of the oligarchs was to hand Athens over to Sparta, and warned the crews that once the oligarchs had won in the city they would abolish the citizenship of the people and then haul the sailors back and dispose of them. Pisander tried to win the crews by first promising to maintain their rations and their arrears of pay, but the sailors turned the terms round and demanded more of him; when the talks broke down, Pisander and his colleagues were killed by the men aboard. In the city, Theramenes was the moderate of the council of Four Hundred, arguing that the coup existed only to force the people to accept a negotiated peace. When the citizen soldiers in the city and the Piraeus rose against the regime, he changed sides at once, urged the Four Hundred to disband, and retired to the altar of the Twelve Gods in the Agora and then to the Acropolis for sanctuary, after which he was included in the general amnesty. Aristophon was likewise a moderate oligarch inclined to avoid bloodshed. On the democratic side stood the crews at Samos, the citizen hoplites who guarded the Acropolis and the Piraeus, and those who argued in the assembly in the Agora for the deposition of the Four Hundred.
kits: 卡面這位「希臘重步兵」在政變裡的份量，遠超一件普通兵器：整場政變的勝負，是由手握長矛與圓盾的公民士兵用集會與集結決定的。公民重步兵的常備裝備是科林斯式或開放面式頭盔、護胸、脛甲、短劍與兩支投擲標槍，行軍用大圓盾（aspis），作戰用兩米長的長矛（dory），槍尾帶銅套；長矛與圓盾一對一互相遮蔽，任何一支隊伍的正面寬度都取決於盾牌有沒有接得上。政變中，衛城守備重步兵是關鍵：他們拒絕聽命於四百人議會的調度，集結在衛城北麓的繆斯神殿一帶，再由比雷埃夫斯港的守軍與水手接應，寡頭派的人被迫退往衛城一隅。除了步戰裝備，這場政變還牽涉海軍裝備：薩摩斯分艦隊由三列槍戰船組成，划槳手與戰士同船，軍餉拖欠正是水手倒戈的直接原因；公元前411年春，雅典在比雷埃夫斯船塢新造約五十艘三列槍戰船準備派往赫勒斯滂，這批新船在政變期間成了雙方都想控制的關鍵資源。寡頭派還計畫在比雷埃夫斯的「聖石」設防、並在衛城駐紮守備，說明城防工事與武器存放處同樣是這場鬥爭的物資基礎。
kitsEn: The weight of the 'Greek hoplite' on the card in this coup far exceeded that of an ordinary weapon: the outcome was settled by citizen soldiers carrying spear and shield, who decided the matter by assembly and by mustering. The ordinary kit of the citizen hoplite was a Corinthian or open-faced helmet, cuirass, greaves, short sword and a pair of throwing javelins, with the great round shield (aspis) on the march and a two-metre spear (dory) in the fight, the spear fitted with a bronze ferrule at its butt; spear and shield covered one another, and the frontage of any body of men depended on whether the shields met. In the coup the hoplites on guard at the Acropolis were the key: they refused to take orders from the council of Four Hundred, gathered round the shrine of the Muses on the northern slope of the Acropolis, and were joined by the garrison of the Piraeus and by the sailors, which forced the oligarchs back into a corner of the hill. Besides the infantry equipment, the coup involved naval material: the squadron at Samos was made up of triremes in which the oarsmen and the soldiers served together, and the arrears of pay were the direct cause of the crews' change of heart; in the spring of 411 BC the Athenians built some fifty new triremes in the Piraeus yards for service in the Hellespont, and these new ships became the asset that both sides wanted to control during the coup. The oligarchs also planned to fortify the Sacred Rock in the Piraeus and to station a garrison on the Acropolis, which shows that the fortifications and the store of arms were the material base of the struggle.
tactics: 寡頭派這一方用的是政變式的戰術，全套動作都圍繞「誰控制武裝的公民」展開。陰謀在城內的聚會（synedria）與陶匠區的私宅中醞釀，交換誓盟的地點是廣場的十二神祭壇；奪權之後，四百人議會立刻廢除五百人議會、接管議事堂，改以抽籤恢復五百人議會，並指定十人籌劃委員會為「五千人」量身訂立憲制，同時宣布在比雷埃夫斯的聖石設防、派兵駐衛城，試圖用城防與守備隊把反對者隔開。同時派皮山德赴薩摩斯島，讓水手解散、繳械返航，釜底抽薪地斷掉民主派最後的武力支點。但水手不肯聽令，反而選出代表、要求由「五千人」掌權並補發軍餉，把「城內政變」變成「海上叛變」。民主派的反制同樣是軍事化的：駐衛城的重步兵拒絕交接防務，比雷埃夫斯港的守軍與水手會合，全城公民在集市集會，一致拒絕承認四百人議會，並在反對派退出議事堂後重組五百人議會、恢復抽籤與議事規則。溫和派在關鍵時刻轉向，寡頭派失去領導權，退守衛城與祭壇，最後由城邦處置。這裡的「陣形」不是方陣，而是集合點、議事堂、祭壇、港口與衛城五個控制點的爭奪。
tacticsEn: The oligarchs fought with the methods of a coup, and every step turned on who controlled the armed citizens. The plot was hatched in political clubs and in private houses in the quarter of the potters, and the oaths were exchanged at the altar of the Twelve Gods in the Agora. Once they had taken power, the Four Hundred at once abolished the Council of Five Hundred, took over the Council House, restored a council of five hundred chosen by lot, and appointed ten commissioners to frame a constitution for the Five Thousand; they also announced that the Sacred Rock in the Piraeus was to be fortified and troops posted to the Acropolis, in the hope of cutting the opposition off with walls and garrisons. At the same time Pisander was sent to Samos to get the crews to disband and give up their arms, so as to cut the last armed prop from under the democrats. The crews would not hear it: they chose their own representatives, demanded that the Five Thousand should govern and that arrears of pay be settled, and turned a coup in the city into a mutiny at sea. The counter-move of the democrats was just as militarised: the hoplites on guard at the Acropolis refused to hand over their posts, the garrison of the Piraeus joined the sailors, and the citizens of the city assembled in the Agora to refuse any recognition of the Four Hundred; after the oligarchs withdrew from the Council House, the Council of Five Hundred was reconstituted with lot and with the old rules of procedure. The moderates turned at the decisive moment, the oligarchs lost their leadership, and retreated to the Acropolis and the altar, where the city finally disposed of them. The 'formation' in this case was not a phalanx but a struggle over five control points: the muster points, the Council House, the altar, the harbour and the Acropolis.
data: 這場政變的可靠數字不多，絕大多數出自修昔底德《伯羅奔尼撒戰爭史》第八卷九十六至九十九章。奪權方是「四百人議會」，按十個部落各出四十人組成；對手一方提出的是「五千人」名冊，寡頭派另指定十人籌劃委員會起草憲制。政變同時逼近雅典的兩支主力兵力：城內與比雷埃夫斯港的公民重步兵，以及駐紮薩摩斯島的雅典海軍。薩摩斯分艦隊的規模在六十艘上下，其中一部分是公元前411年春在比雷埃夫斯新造的約五十艘三列槍戰船，隨船的水手與划槳手已多時未支軍餉。寡頭統治的時間約四個月，學界一般定於公元前411年9月至12月之間；修昔底德提到政變期間曾出現月食，可作斷代錨點，但對應的具體日期仍有不同推算。政變平定之後，民主派把「五千人」名冊擴為「一萬一千人」，並由忒拉美涅斯主持立法，赦免政變首謀，只追究極端派。
dataEn: Reliable figures for this coup are few, and nearly all of them come from chapters 96 to 99 of the eighth book of Thucydides' History of the Peloponnesian War. Those who seized power were the council of Four Hundred, forty members from each of the ten tribes; against them the democrats put forward a list of Five Thousand, and the oligarchs named ten commissioners to draw up the constitution. The coup was brought to bear on the two armed forces of Athens at once: the citizen hoplites in the city and the Piraeus, and the Athenian fleet stationed at Samos. The Samos squadron numbered around sixty sail, including some of the fifty new triremes built at the Piraeus in the spring of 411 BC, and the crews and oarsmen had long gone without pay. The oligarchy lasted about four months, which is generally placed between September and December of 411 BC; Thucydides mentions a lunar eclipse during the coup, which can serve as an anchor for the dating, though the exact day remains a matter of calculation. After the coup was settled, the democrats widened the list of the Five Thousand into the Eleven Thousand, and Theramenes presided over the legislation that pardoned the leaders of the coup and reserved prosecution for the extremists.
cause: 直接導火線是公元前413年西西里遠征全軍覆沒之後的連續崩潰：雅典損失了主力戰艦、數萬人命與大筆儲備，帝國的貢金收入幾乎斷絕，斯巴達聯軍自同年起在狄刻利亞設長期據點，切斷阿提卡的鄉村收入與勞里翁銀礦，雅典只剩下城牆與海軍兩件武器。久戰、疫病與饑荒累積的疲憊，讓城內出現一種「無論誰執政都打不下去」的絕望情緒，議會中要求談和的呼聲越來越高。陰謀者以「為了能議和、為了停止流血」作為旗幟，把和談破裂的責任歸於民主派與其將領，並聲稱民主本身才是無秩序的根源。次一級的原因是內部的派系裂痕：五百人議會與陪審法庭之中，富裕公民與平民代表長期互相猜忌，寡頭派自認有錢、有戰功、有修辭本領，認為由划槳手組成的民主只配在前線流血。而在雅典的盟邦與敵方眼中，流傳著民主派正打算把雅典城拱手讓給斯巴達的消息，這一傳聞成為陰謀者最好的說服工具：亞西比德的書信、薩摩斯水手的懷疑、衛城守兵的猶疑，都建立在「寡頭派要出賣城邦」這個前提上。此外，軍餉拖欠、戰艦閒置、指揮權爭奪與個人恩怨的摩擦，讓水手與守備在政變臨近時都成了可以被拉攏的對象。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the chain of collapses that followed the destruction of the Sicilian expedition in 413 BC: Athens had lost the main body of her warships, tens of thousands of men and a large part of her reserves, the tribute of the empire had almost ceased, and from that same year the Spartan coalition held a permanent base at Decelea, cutting off the rural income of Attica and the silver of the Laurium mines, so that only the walls and the fleet remained to Athens. The weariness of a long war, with plague and famine on top of it, produced a mood of despair in the city, in which men felt that whoever governed the city would not be able to end the war; the demand for negotiations grew louder in the assembly. The conspirators carried the banner of wanting to be able to make peace and wanting the shedding of blood to stop, blamed the democracy and its generals for the failure of the armistice, and argued that democracy itself was the source of disorder. A secondary cause was the factional split inside the city: in the Council of Five Hundred and the jury courts the richer citizens and the popular representatives distrusted one another for years, and the oligarchs considered that they had the money, the war record and the gift of speech, while a democracy of oarsmen was fit to bleed at the front line only. In the eyes of the Athenian allies and of the enemy alike, a rumour circulated that the democrats were about to hand the city of Athens over to Sparta, and this rumour became the conspirators' most useful instrument of persuasion: the letter of Alcibiades, the suspicions of the crews at Samos and the hesitations of the Acropolis guard all rested on the premise that the oligarchs were about to sell out the city. Arrears of pay, idle warships, quarrels over command and personal rivalries made the crews and the garrison into people who could be won over on the eve of the coup.
impact: 政變雖然失敗，卻在雅典民主的體質上留下了幾道深痕。第一，寡頭派提出的「祖傳政體」，即把權力交給若干被選出的賢者、恢復審慎法治的說法，從此成為雅典政治論述中一條長壽的支線：前410年民主復辟時「一萬一千人」名冊的設計，乃至公元前404年三十人執政的憲制，都可以在這次政變中找到雛形；此後每一次政變者都會援引梭倫的名義，聲稱自己在恢復祖制。第二，政變的過程讓雅典公民兵第一次體會到自身的武裝是一種政治力量，也讓城邦明白：只要軍隊駐在薩摩斯、只要城內守備握在重步兵手裡，議會的決議就必須靠武力才落得下去。第三，民主派從此學會以赦免換取安寧，前410年的「一萬一千人」名冊與大赦即是這次危機的直接產物，雅典民主由公民大會、五百人議會與陪審法庭三者構成的格局也在此後固定下來。第四，就戰爭而言，這場政變在最要緊的時候消耗了寶貴的時間與士氣：前411年派往赫勒斯滂的四千重步兵與五十艘新船，正是政變風波中籌劃的兵力，最終在羊河與基齊庫斯的失敗中耗盡，斯巴達的霸權在隨後十年間逐步成形。
impactEn: The coup failed, but it left deep marks on the constitution of Athenian democracy. First, the oligarchs' formula of the ancestral constitution, the claim to hand power to a number of selected worthies and to restore orderly rule, became a long-lived line of Athenian political argument from that moment on: the design of the list of the Eleven Thousand after the democracy was restored in 410 BC, and even the constitution of the Thirty in 404 BC, can all be traced back to this coup, and every later conspirator invoked the name of Solon to claim that he was restoring ancestral custom. Second, the course of the coup taught the Athenian citizens for the first time that their own arms were a political force, and taught the city that as long as the fleet sat at Samos and the hoplites in the city held their shields, the decrees of the assembly had to be enforced by force. Third, the democrats learned to buy peace with pardon: the list of the Eleven Thousand and the general amnesty of 410 BC were the direct product of this crisis, and the shape of Athenian democracy as a trio of assembly, Council of Five Hundred and jury courts was fixed from that point. Fourth, in the war itself the coup consumed time and morale at the most expensive moment: the four thousand hoplites and the fifty new ships sent to the Hellespont in 411 BC were the very forces being organised amid the political crisis, and they were spent in the defeats at Abydos and Cyzicus, so that Spartan hegemony could take shape over the following decade.
result: 政變以失敗告終。公元前411年12月，四百人議會在城內公民重步兵與比雷埃夫斯港守軍的抵制下失去民意與武力，市集集會上主張廢黜它的聲音佔了多數，議會自行解散，五百人議會恢復，寡頭派的重要人物退往衛城與廣場的十二神祭壇尋求庇護，其後一部分被拘禁、一部分被處決、一部分流亡；主張溫和的忒拉美涅斯與阿里斯托豐列名赦免名單，得以留在城內，並在往後十年間先後出任公職。在薩摩斯島，皮山德與同來的寡頭使者被水手殺死，這一事件坐實了「寡頭派會出賣海軍」的傳說，也讓亞西比德的影響力重新回到雅典。政變平定後，民主派在公元前410年把「五千人」名冊擴充為「一萬一千人」，並頒布追究陰謀者的法律。雅典保住了城牆與民主的框架，卻沒有因此扭轉戰局：往後數年海軍在赫勒斯滂與愛琴海連敗，前405年伊奧斯波塔米失守之後，公元前404年雅典投降、三十人執政上台，政變的教訓最終以更嚴酷的形式被重新學了一遍。
resultEn: The coup ended in failure. In December 411 BC the Four Hundred lost both consent and the means of coercion before the citizen hoplites of the city and the garrison of the Piraeus; in the assembly in the Agora the voices calling for their deposition were in the majority, the council dissolved itself, the Council of Five Hundred was restored, and the leading oligarchs withdrew to the Acropolis and to the altar of the Twelve Gods in the Agora for sanctuary, after which some were imprisoned, some executed and some went into exile. The moderates Theramenes and Aristophon were placed on the list of pardoned men, stayed in the city and in the following ten years held public office in turn. At Samos, Pisander and the oligarchic envoys who had come with him were killed by the crews, an event that confirmed the story that the oligarchs would sell out the fleet and that restored Alcibiades' influence in Athens. Once the coup had been settled, the democrats widened the list of the Five Thousand into the Eleven Thousand in 410 BC and passed a law directed at the conspirators. Athens saved its walls and the framework of its democracy, but it did not thereby turn the war: the fleet lost at sea in the Hellespont and the Aegean in the years that followed, and after Aegospotami in 405 BC Athens surrendered in 404 BC and the Thirty took power, so that the lesson of the coup was learned once more in a harsher form.
